<explanation>
1. Project Type and Purpose  
   - This is an open-source, multi-component .NET tool (GitVersion) that computes Semantic Version numbers from Git history.  
   - Key outputs include:  
     • A cross-platform CLI application (“GitVersion.Tool”)  
     • A .NET API/core library (“GitVersion.Core”)  
     • MSBuild tasks integration (“GitVersion.MsBuild”)  
     • Various output modules (AssemblyInfo, Wix, JSON, etc.)  
     • Docker images, Homebrew/Chocolatey packages, and GitHub Actions integration  

2. High-Level Architecture Overview  
   - Split the diagram into two main domains:  
     A. Runtime components (the library, tools, and extensions)  
     B. CI/CD & Packaging pipeline  

3. Identify Main Components (Runtime Domain)  
   a. Frontends  
      – CLI Application (GitVersion.App)  
      – MSBuild Task (GitVersion.MsBuild)  
      – New-CLI generator (`new-cli` folder)  
   b. Core Engine  
      – GitVersion.Core (version calculation, branch strategies, deployment modes)  
      – Configuration Provider (GitVersion.Configuration)  
      – Build Agent Resolver (GitVersion.BuildAgents)  
      – Git abstraction layer (GitVersion.LibGit2Sharp)  
   c. Output Modules (GitVersion.Output)  
      – AssemblyInfo generator  
      – Project file updater  
      – Wix file updater  
      – JSON/console serializers  
   d. Schema Generator (GitVersion.Schema)  
   e. Testing Harness (GitVersion.Testing & various *.Tests projects)  

4. External Dependencies  
   - Git repository on local file system (via LibGit2Sharp)  
   - Environment variables / Build Server APIs (Azure Pipelines, GitHub Actions, Jenkins, etc.)  
   - Package registries: NuGet, Chocolatey, Homebrew, DockerHub  
   - CI services: GitHub Actions, Azure Pipelines  

5. Relationships and Data Flows  
   - User invokes CLI or MSBuild Task →  
     • CLI/MSBuild passes command-line args to Argument Parser →  
     • Configuration Provider reads YAML/JSON files →  
     • Build Agent Resolver detects CI environment →  
     • Core Engine (GitVersion.Core) uses LibGit2Sharp to scan Git history →  
     • Calculation modules apply version strategies →  
     • Core outputs version data to Output Modules →  
     • Output Modules write files or print JSON/console output →  
     • CLI/MSBuild returns exit code  
   - Schema Generator produces JSON schemas for configuration.  
   - Test projects invoke core and modules via in-memory or virtual repos.

6. CI/CD & Packaging Pipeline Components  
   - Workflow triggers: GitHub Actions / Azure Pipelines  
   - Build orchestrator: Cake scripts (in `build/*`)  
     • Tasks: restore, build solution, run tests, generate docs, package CLI, Docker images  
   - Artifact publishing:  
     • NuGet (GitVersion.Tool, GitVersion.MsBuild)  
     • Chocolatey (GitVersion.Portable)  
     • Homebrew formula  
     • Docker Hub images  
     • GitHub Releases  

7. Architectural Patterns & Principles  
   - Modular design with clear separation of concerns: CLI vs. Core vs. Output  
   - Dependency Injection (modules wired via IContainer)  
   - Abstraction layers for Git (via LibGit2Sharp) and Build Agents  
   - Strategy pattern for version calculation (multiple IVersionStrategy implementations)  

8. Diagramming Guidelines  
   a. Use clear labels for each component box (e.g., “GitVersion.Core”, “GitVersion.App”, “CLI Parser”, “Output: AssemblyInfo”)  
   b. Color code by component type:  
      – Blue for frontends (CLI, MSBuild)  
      – Green for core engine/configuration  
      – Orange for output modules  
      – Gray for external services (Git, CI/CD, registries)  
   c. Draw directional arrows to show:  
      – Invocation flow (CLI → Parser → Core → Output)  
      – Data flow (Git repo → Core Engine → Output Modules)  
      – CI/CD flow (Repo → CI service → Build scripts → Artifacts → Registries)  
   d. Group related projects into containers or swimlanes (Runtime vs. Build & Release)  
   e. Annotate important library/framework names (.NET, LibGit2Sharp, Cake, GitHub Actions)  

9. Tailoring Tips for This Project  
   - Emphasize that this is a CLI-first architecture, not a microservices or web app.  
   - Show how multiple consumers (CLI, MSBuild, Docker, Homebrew) reuse the same core library.  
   - In the CI/CD section, highlight how Cake tasks invoke build, test, docs, packaging, and publishing in sequence.  

10. Final Notes  
   - Capture every major folder under `src/` as a component.  
   - Do not over-complicate: show modules only at a level that conveys clear separation (no need to show every *.cs file).  
   - The goal is to depict how code flows from user input through core and out to files/services, and how the build pipeline automates packaging and release.  
</explanation>
